title: Ned's Rainy Day Dam
checkpoint: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — review of split digraphs and early alternative pronunciations (y as igh/ee, a as o, e as ee).
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — review of split digraphs and early alternative pronunciations (y as igh/ee, a as o, e as ee).

pages.text: Ned wants a dam in the stream.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling standing at the edge of a small stream, looking at the flowing water with purpose.

pages.text: Ned gets smooth stones off the bank.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling picking up smooth round stones from the muddy bank of the stream.

pages.text: Ned sets the stones in a line.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling arranging a line of stones across the narrow stream.

pages.text: The stream tugs a stone away.
pages.illustration: A single stone tumbling away from the line, pulled by the moving water.

pages.text: Ned gets a big flat stone.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling picking up one large, flat grey stone, bigger than the others.

pages.text: Ned packs mud round the stones.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling pressing wet mud into the gaps between the stones with his beak.
Raindrops dotting the surface of the stream around Ned and his stone dam.

pages.text: The dam sits firm in the rain.
pages.illustration: Water calmly pooling up behind the dam of stones, the flow slowed to a trickle on the other side.

pages.text: A snug pool sits next to Ned.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling sitting proudly beside a small calm pool of water held back by his dam.

pages.text: Ned has a pool for a rainy day.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling floating happily on his new still pool as the rain falls gently around him.
